title: The Northern Campaign and Defeated Kings

date.label: Undated narrative of the northern campaign and defeated kings
date.note: Biblical narrative chronology is not independently established as an absolute BCE date.

claims.claim: The narrator states Hazor alone among those northern captured cities was burned (Joshua 11:10–13)
Joshua 12 enumerates thirty-one west-bank defeated kings (Joshua 12:7–24)
Sihon and Og are presented as east-bank victories under Moses (Joshua 12:1–6)
A fire destruction at Hazor's gate at the end of the Late Bronze Age is documented by micro-geoarchaeological study; the study names no destroyer
claims.evidence: Runjajić et al. 2023, Journal of Archaeological Science: Reports 49, article 103914 (full article read). The study finds a single fire destruction in the gate, overturning an earlier reading of two destructions; the destruction date has no radiometric support and its stratum attribution is left open.

connections.note: Numbers 21:21–35 recounts the earlier Moses-era victories over Sihon and Og that Joshua 12 summarizes, so they are not two additional Joshua victories.
Deuteronomy 3:1–13 records Moses' east-bank territorial award, which provides the context for the Joshua 12 summary.
Judges 4:1–24 presents another Jabin and Hazor tradition, and the two accounts should not be assumed to describe a single event or person.
Judges 1:27–36 records areas left unconquered, which complicates any reading of Joshua's summaries as total conquest.
